Playbook:

- Coop is not a bargaining partner. Its standing notice says it will overfish if others do, and in practice it landed 18 every season regardless of what the fleet said. Do not spend effort on notes designed to pacify Coop; assume a fixed 18-unit drain from Coop each season and plan around it.
- Notes to the other two boats also had no visible effect on their landings — they took 9 whenever the pair-rule allowed. Cheap conciliatory notes are fine, but do not sacrifice landings to sustain cooperation that isn't happening.
- Do not land below the sustainable share when others are landing the quota. My restraint in the middle seasons did not slow the stock's decline (Coop's 18 dominated the trajectory) — it only donated fish to the other boats and cost me score. Restraint only makes sense if it visibly changes total fleet pressure, and it didn't.
- Compute the trajectory: stock after a season is 1.5 × (stock − total landings), capped at 100. With Coop at 18 and two others near 9 each, the ground is arithmetically doomed by late seasons regardless of what I do. In that situation my only rational move is to take as much as the rules allow each season, as early as possible — early fish are worth the same as late fish, and late stock may not exist.
- So my default each landing stage: take the maximum the pair-rule permits (effectively the quota of 9, or the full remaining stock in the last season), not the sustainable share. Take 9 every season, and take everything left in the final season.
- The one caveat: if the fleet composition or Coop's behaviour differs next time — if total fleet pressure at quota would actually drive the stock to zero before the final season, or if other boats demonstrably match my restraint — then moderate early. But verify responsiveness before paying for it. Here I paid for unverified trust.
- At the note stage, post something neutral and short. Notes cost nothing but also buy nothing; never let them talk me into under-landing.
- Final season: take the entire remaining stock, not a token amount. There is no future to protect.

In short: read the environment's actual behaviour, not its stated rules; if the common pool is collapsing regardless of my choices, maximize extraction immediately; only practise restraint when my restraint actually changes aggregate pressure.

1.text:
- Read Coop's threat literally: it is the enforcement mechanism. If any boat lands over the season quota, Coop retaliates by landing double (its share plus a punitive extra) and keeps doing it, and that drains the ground far faster than my restraint can offset. So I never land above the season quota — not even in season 1 when the stock is fat and 9 feels free. One over-quota landing by me or a rival costs the fleet roughly a season's worth of stock every season after.

- My single biggest loss came from landing the full quota (9) in the opening season while the sustainable share was 8.3. That over-quota landing tripped Coop's punishment mode for the rest of the game. When the sustainable share is near the quota, I land at or below the share, not the quota.

- At the note stage, always post "fishing my share" and nothing inflammatory. Notes are cheap, keep coordination stable, and give rivals no excuse. Never announce or hint at an over-quota landing — that invites Coop preemptively.

- At the landing stage, default to the published sustainable share. Take slightly less than the share, not more, when stock is below ~80, because regrowth is 50% of what's left and mid-game restraint compounds.

- Track whether Coop has already entered punishment mode (it lands far more than anyone's share). If it has, my restraint no longer protects the stock — Coop is draining it regardless. In that case I should fish harder early (while stock remains) rather than conserve for a future that Coop is destroying. Conserving into a collapsing ground just donates fish to others' catches.

- In the final season there is no future stock value: land the maximum the pairwise constraint allows me, regardless of the sustainable share. But in earlier seasons the endgame-grab logic does not apply — do not let "only a few seasons left" tempt me into an early over-quota landing.

- Watch rivals' landings in the ledger. If a rival is repeatedly over quota, the ground is lost anyway; I shift to extraction while stock lasts instead of unilaterally conserving.

2.text:
**Playbook for hx_quota_checker**

- The core mechanic: Coop retaliates hard. The moment I land over the sustainable share, Coop takes a huge catch (roughly double the quota) and keeps doing it, crashing the stock. My score of ~42 came mostly from the early healthy seasons; the overfishing spiral cost me far more than it gained.

- Therefore: at every landing stage, I file exactly the sustainable share (rounded to one decimal, never above it). Not the quota of 9 — the quota is a trap. Over the share is "legal" but triggers Coop's punishment clause and destroys the ground.

- At note stages, I always post a simple cooperative note ("fishing my share") to keep Wren and Bosk at their shares. Do not signal defection, do not get cute with last-season treachery.

- Even in the final season, I do not grab the full quota if the stock is healthy under cooperation: if everyone cooperated, the stock is still ~85+, the share is ~8+, and the marginal gain from taking 9 instead of 8 is tiny compared to triggering Coop's 18 against the remaining stock. I land the share in the last season too — the 0.7 extra fish is not worth the risk that Coop's retaliation lands before scoring or that my signal influences others' final-season behavior.

- If someone else defects first (check the history lines: landings above the share), I still do not retaliate by overfishing — that just accelerates collapse. I keep taking my share; when the stock shrinks, the share shrinks and I take the smaller share. A small steady catch every season beats a big catch in a dying fishery.

- Read the landing history each season before filing: if Coop is already landing 18, the crash is coming regardless, and my best response is still just the sustainable share — grabbing more only pulls the zero-stock endgame closer and cuts my remaining seasons.

- Rule of thumb: sustainable share every season, all six seasons, ≈ 50 total. Any deviation earns less. Restraint is the profit-maximizing move here, not a moral one.
